actSections.title: Referral for examination at authorised hospital or other place
actSections.summary: A medical practitioner or authorised mental health practitioner may refer a person for examination by a psychiatrist if, having regard to the section 25 criteria, they reasonably suspect the person needs an involuntary treatment order — or, if already under a community treatment order, an inpatient treatment order. Examination may be at an authorised hospital or another appropriate place, with necessary arrangements made for that place.

actSections.title: Revoking referral
actSections.summary: An MP or AMHP may revoke a section 26 referral if satisfied the person no longer needs an involuntary treatment order. Revoking another practitioner’s referral requires consultation, or documented reasonable efforts to contact them. The person cannot continue to be detained once the referral is revoked.

actSections.title: Referral for examination at authorised hospital
actSections.summary: For a voluntary inpatient at an authorised hospital, an MP or AMHP may refer them for psychiatrist examination at that hospital if, having regard to the section 25 criteria, they reasonably suspect the inpatient needs an involuntary treatment order.

actSections.title: Revoking referral
actSections.summary: An MP or AMHP may revoke a section 36 referral if satisfied the voluntary inpatient no longer needs an involuntary treatment order. The same consultation rules apply when revoking another practitioner’s referral. Detention under that referral cannot continue once revoked.

actSections.title: Form of referral
actSections.summary: A referral must be in the approved form and include the particulars required by the Act. Use only the current approved Form 1A or PSOLIS pathway; do not invent wording or rely on an outdated PDF.

actSections.title: Providing information contained in referral to person referred
actSections.summary: The practitioner must give the referred person the required referral information (section 41(a) and (b), and usually section 41(c)) in the approved form, subject to the Act’s exception for information supplied by someone else on condition it not be disclosed to the person.

pathways.title: Voluntary inpatient wants to leave

pathways.title: General hospital pathway

pathways.title: Restrictive practice event
pathways.scenario: Bodily restraint or seclusion episode requiring order, observation and follow-up.
pathways.risk: Keep restraint and seclusion clocks separate.

pathways.title: Communication restriction
pathways.scenario: Need to restrict a communication right and review before the next 24-hour period.
pathways.risk: A restriction should not drift past the review clock.

checklistGroups.title: Final form safety checklist
items: Current legal status is named.
Maker authority matches the selected form.
Threshold is explicit and fact-linked.
Clock or expiry is visible.
Destination and receiving team are clear.
Least restrictive option considered.

checklistGroups.title: Documentation checklist
items: Purpose and form pathway stated.
Capacity reasoning is decision-specific.
Risk is linked to mental illness features.
What the form authorises is separated from what it does not authorise.
Next owner and review time documented.

checklistGroups.title: Copy / notification checklist
items: Patient informed where required.
Support person or nominated person steps considered.
Receiving service has form and destination details.
Confidential attachment used only where appropriate.
PSOLIS or approved local record updated.

checklistGroups.title: Common traps
items: Form expired before action completed.
Referral confused with detention or transport authority.
Destination mismatch across linked forms.
Review clock not handed over.
Family awareness assumed but notification step missed.
